photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: A woman poses in a beaded dress, shawl with geometric beadwork, and holds two decorated bags, photographed at Lapwai, Idaho (a Nez Perce community); this documentary photo clearly shows Nez Perce traditional dress and craftwork.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a named Nez Perce chief wearing decorated hide tunic, leggings, moccasins, shell choker, and fur headdress, holding a feather fan and pipe — a documentary photograph of Nez Perce dress.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: A Nez Perce woman photographed in traditional beaded dress, belt, and holding beaded bags outside a house in Lapwai, Idaho — a documentary photo of dress and craft matching the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Timothy (Tomoson), a documented Nez Perce chief, wearing fringed hide tunic and leggings, shell/bear-claw choker, feathered headband, and holding a pipe — a documentary photo of dress consistent with the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Jason (Kol-kol-shu-a-tash), a named Nez Perce chief, in decorated hide tunic, leggings, moccasins, shell choker and fur headdress, seated beside a non-Native companion; clearly documents Nez Perce dress.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: A Nez Perce woman in Lapwai, Idaho poses in traditional beaded buckskin dress with woven cornhusk bags, a documentary photo consistent with Nez Perce material culture.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Timothy, a Nez Perce chief, wearing decorated fringed hide tunic, leggings, moccasins, shell/bear-claw choker, and feathered headband — documentary dress photo of the named ethnicity, alongside an Anglo companion in a suit.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: The photograph shows Timothy (Tomoson), a Nez Perce chief, in a historical studio portrait. It is documentary evidence of a Nez Perce person, though his Western suit is not distinctive Nez Perce material culture.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Lawyer (Hal-al-ho-sote), a named Nez Perce man, wearing a Western suit but with a beaded/embroidered pouch worn across his torso — a documentary photo of a Nez Perce individual's dress.

household.name: Bowcase-quiver
household.title: Bowcase and Quiver
household.reason: This is a beaded and quilled bowcase-and-quiver set with otter fur trailers and beaded geometric patterning, a classic Plateau-region hunting accessory used by the Nez Perce for carrying bow and arrows.

household.name: bag, cornhusk bag, bag
household.title: bag, cornhusk bag, bag
household.reason: A classic cornhusk (corn husk/hemp) twined bag with geometric X-motif designs, documented as a gift from a named Nez Perce woman in Kamiah, Idaho — a well-known Plateau Nez Perce craft form.

household.name: korg, basket
household.title: korg, basket
household.reason: A coiled twined basket with imbricated geometric designs in dark red/black/white, consistent with Plateau (Nez Perce) basketry traditions and handles typical of such carrying baskets.

household.name: baby-carrier
household.title: baby-carrier
household.reason: The image shows a traditional deerskin cradleboard/baby-carrier with a beaded panel in geometric cross motifs, a classic Plateau-style (Nez Perce) infant carrier construction.

household.name: purse; wallet
household.title: purse; wallet
household.reason: A corn-husk twined purse with glass-bead strap, a craft form well documented among Plateau peoples including the Nez Perce; the embroidered rose is a common commercial-era motif but the object type and technique match the attribution.

household.name: bag
household.title: bag
household.reason: A cornhusk twined bag with classic diamond/zigzag geometric pattern, a well-documented Plateau craft made by the Nez Perce; museum confirms maker attribution.

household.name: bag; wallet
household.title: bag; wallet
household.reason: A twined cornhusk wallet bag with geometric wool overlay designs, a classic Plateau-region (Nez Perce) utilitarian container made from corn husk, hemp twine, wool yarn and deerskin trim. This matches well-documented Nez Perce material culture.

household.name: bag
household.title: bag
household.reason: A twined corn-husk/hemp flat storage bag with classic geometric triangle designs, a well-known Nez Perce/Plateau craft form (often called a "sally bag" or cornhusk bag), matching the museum's attribution.

household.name: bag
household.title: bag
household.reason: This is a twined cornhusk/grass storage bag with a classic geometric zigzag design in false embroidery, a well-known Plateau (Nez Perce) basketry-weaving tradition.

textile.name: bag
textile.title: bag
textile.reason: The image shows a cornhusk/fiber twined flat bag with classic geometric triangle and diamond designs in a style characteristic of Plateau peoples like the Nez Perce, with red trade-cloth reinforced edges typical of these bags.

textile.name: bag
textile.title: bag
textile.reason: This is a classic cornhusk/hemp twined flat bag with a diamond/checkered geometric pattern, a well-known Nez Perce (Plateau) woven storage bag form, matching the museum's attribution.

textile.name: bag
textile.title: bag
textile.reason: A cornhusk/hemp twined flat bag with geometric false-embroidery designs, a classic Plateau (Nez Perce) type of woven storage/flat bag, consistent with the claimed makers.
